newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate down on pre-auction demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate down on pre-auction demand.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down 50 basis points to 17.50 percent in early trade on Tuesday due to demand from dealers ahead of expected forthcoming cuts in primary rates, traders said.
"They're buying on forecast rate cuts at the primary auction, they want to buy at good levels," a trader said.
Dealers said they predicted falls of up to 100 basis points on bellwether 28-day Cetes at the central bank auction of government securities to be held later in the day.
Analysts said recent falls in U.S. long bond yields had also driven forecasts of domestic rate cuts.
"The peso is firm, very quiet and the U.S. long bond is still at favorable levels," one analyst said.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was meanwhile off 5/32 to yield 6.89 percent. Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 3.3 centavos firmer in early trade at 7.8740/7.8770 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper had fallen 70 basis points to 18.50 percent in early trade.
Liquidity of 1.725 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
